text:
Jordan (Customer): Hey team — we've got a customer on Dedicated who says users removed in Okta are still able to access the Redwood Console and call the API. They show the SCIM delete events went through on their side. Can you help?
Priya (CSE): Thanks for flagging. Quick q: are they using group-to-role mappings or per-user role provisioning?
Jordan (Customer): Group->role mapping. They removed a user from the "Platform Admins" group at 09:12 UTC but the user still sees admin routes and can create API keys.
Priya (CSE): Oof. Any SCIM logs / provisioning request IDs from their Okta side?
Jordan (Customer): They provided a webhook delivery log: scim PATCH to /Users/3b9c... with operations remove, status 200. They also attached our webhook response: 200 OK but body is empty.
Samir (ENG): That empty body is suspicious. Our SCIM handler usually returns 204 for delete or a full JSON. Which component handled that webhook — private control plane or customer on-prem connector?
Priya (CSE): It's Private (VPC) with a control-plane proxy. They said they use our SCIM token (scim-sync token) created last quarter.
Luis (IAM): Quick check: token scopes for SCIM tokens are fine normally, but if the token is rotated or missing the "provision:write" scope we could accept the webhook then silently skip role unlinking. Can the customer paste the Authorization header (redact token) and the response trace id?
Jordan (Customer): Header: Authorization: Bearer REDACTED; trace_id: t-9f3a21. They said token was created with a partner script, not through the console UI.
Mika (Product): Partner scripts historically used the older "scim.basic" scope which only allowed user creates/updates but not group sync. If the token lacks group scope we might apply the user status change but not run the group->role reconciliation.
Samir (ENG): I pulled the logs for t-9f3a21. The SCIM v2 endpoint receives the PATCH, we call the provisioning worker which enqueues a job, the job completes with success, but the group-sync step early-returns because the token metadata resolves to scope: ["users:write"]. So we don't strip roles.
Priya (CSE): That matches customer report exactly. Any idea how token lost scope? They said no rotation.
Luis (IAM): Possible: token was created via API using legacy grant and the permissions service was later hardened; the token's scope mapping didn't get the "groups:write" flag. We should show them how to inspect token metadata.
Jordan (Customer): Is there a safe remediation they can do now to remove admin rights while we patch?
Priya (CSE): Two options: 1) Manual revoke of the API keys for that user via Admin -> API keys (fast). 2) Re-run a forced full sync from their Okta side (group push) which will hit our /Groups endpoint — but that will still be skipped if scope missing. So only revoking keys is immediate.
Samir (ENG): I'll add a temporary reconciliation endpoint that ignores token scope for a single request with an explicit admin override header (X-Admin-Override: true) — but that requires eng approval because it bypasses RBAC.
Mika (Product): Before we do that, can we do a safer path: create a one-time scoped SCIM token for them with groups:write and ask them to re-run the group push? That avoids touching RBAC.
Luis (IAM): I can mint a one-time token that expires in 1 hour and has explicit scopes: ["users:write","groups:write","provision:admin"]. Will need the customer's org id to bind.
Jordan (Customer): Org id: redwood-acme-42. They prefer the one-time token method.
Priya (CSE): I'll send the one-time token via the secure channel and instruct them to perform a full group push and then confirm. Also ask them to redact any tokens before posting.
Jordan (Customer): Got the token, ran the group push at 10:03 UTC. They say users were removed from admin role on our side and API keys invalidated. Confirmed for the initial user.
Samir (ENG): Thanks. Root cause summary: existing SCIM token lacked the groups:write scope due to legacy provisioning API usage. Our provisioning worker accepted incoming SCIM requests but skipped group->role reconciliation when scope didn't include groups write.
Mika (Product): Action items: 1) Improve SCIM webhook 200 semantics — return explicit JSON with applied operations and scope-check warnings (low effort). 2) Add an admin-facing token inspector in Console to show scopes and creation method. 3) Longer-term: make group reconciliation log a visible audit event so customers can see "group removal processed" vs "skipped due to token scope".
Samir (ENG): I'll open an internal bug and a safe hotfix plan: detect tokens without groups:write and return 403 with a message on the SCIM response for future requests. That will cause Okta to surface a failed sync (preferred).
Luis (IAM): I'll also add a one-time rotation API for customers that creates properly-scoped temporary tokens for emergency recon.
Priya (CSE): I'll follow up with the customer with the postmortem and the mitigation steps. Jordan, can you confirm if they want a RFC for changing the partner script?
Jordan (Customer): Yes — they want a recommended patch to their provisioning script and a note for their SSO team. Thanks everyone! :thumbsup:
